skuLines.line: Kachi ghani mustard oil — 1 L pouch (mass brand)
skuLines.examples: Fortune Premium Kachi Ghani 1 L, Dhara Kachi Ghani 1 L, Patanjali Kachi Ghani 1 L, Emami Healthy & Tasty 1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; uplift Nov–Feb (sarson da saag, warming food, baby massage)
skuLines.notes: THE core line for this geography — 61% of North-zone households (Delhi/Punjab/J&K/HP/UP) use mustard oil as primary medium. Pouches are 52% of the national mustard market. Never stock a 'mustard blend': FSSAI has banned any multi-source oil containing mustard since 8 Jun 2021. Shelf life 6–9 months (oxidises faster than refined); rotate hard.

skuLines.line: Kachi ghani mustard oil — 1 L PET bottle
skuLines.examples: Fortune Kachi Ghani 1 L bottle, Dhara 1 L bottle, First Crop 1 L bottle
skuLines.notes: Bottle carries a ~₹20–25/L premium over pouch and does not puncture on hill-road transport — stock both formats, pouch for price, bottle for spillage-free carry and reuse.

skuLines.line: Kachi ghani mustard oil — 5 L jar
skuLines.examples: Fortune Mustard Oil 5 L jar, Dhara 5 L, Patanjali 5 L, First Crop 5 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; stock-up before winter break and before monsoon road closures
skuLines.notes: A staff family of 4 runs ~4–5 L cooking oil/month, so this is the natural monthly buy. Heaviest, bulkiest item in the basket — no resident will carry it 30–50 km from town, so ARY's captive share here is near-100%. Offer township home delivery.

skuLines.line: Kachi ghani mustard oil — 15 L / 15 kg institutional tin
skuLines.examples: Fortune 15 L tin, Dhara 15 kg tin, regional Punjab/HP ghani mill tin (Agmark)
skuLines.packSizes: 15 L tin / 15 kg tin (FSSAI cap for sealed packs)
skuLines.priceBand: ₹2,600–3,200 per tin (derived from 5 L pricing, not verified live)
skuLines.seasonality: Follows the academic calendar — collapses during winter and summer vacations
skuLines.notes: The mess / canteen / langar-kitchen line. 15 kg is the legal maximum for a sealed edible-oil pack. Tins dent and rust on ghat roads in heavy monsoon — inspect on receipt, store off the floor on pallets.

skuLines.examples: Fortune 500 ml, Dhara 500 ml, Patanjali 200 ml, Dabur mustard oil 200 ml
skuLines.notes: Bought as much for warm sarson-tel baby massage and head massage as for cooking — a real must-have where married staff have infants. Also the hostel-room / low-cash pack. Keep it on the shelf even though litres are tiny; a missing 200 ml sends a family to town.

skuLines.examples: 24 Mantra Organic cold-pressed mustard, Jivo Kachi Ghani cold press, Anveshan wood-pressed, Two Brothers
skuLines.notes: Fastest-premiumising sub-segment (Indian cold-pressed market ₹755 mn in 2025, ~5.4% CAGR) driven by under-35 'return to roots' rejection of refined oil. Shelf life only 3–6 months and low throughput in a 5,000-person township — stock 1–2 facings, not a wall, or it expires.

skuLines.line: Regional / local ghani mustard oil (value, Agmark-packed)
skuLines.examples: Himachal or Punjab mill brands, HIMFED / co-op packs, Sano, local Agmark ghani tin
skuLines.packSizes: 1 L pouch, 5 L jar, 15 L tin
skuLines.seasonality: Cheapest Mar–May on new mustard crop
skuLines.notes: Price-fighter slot that also carries better margin than the national brands. Must be a sealed, labelled, Agmark pack — loose or repacked oil is prohibited and state FDAs were actively prosecuting in Aug 2026.

skuLines.examples: Fortune Refined Soyabean 1 L / 870 g, First Crop Soyabean 1 L, Nutrela Soyabean, Ruchi
skuLines.notes: The cheapest branded refined oil and the neutral-taste alternative for households that find mustard too pungent — including South Indian and non-North staff at the university.

skuLines.examples: Fortune Soyabean 5 L / 4.35 kg jar, First Crop 5 L, Nutrela 5 L
skuLines.notes: Note the weight-declared 4.35 kg jar sells as a '5 litre' — shelf-tag price per litre so residents can compare honestly against town rates.

skuLines.line: Refined soyabean oil — 15 kg institutional tin
skuLines.examples: Fortune 15 kg tin, Ruchi 15 kg tin, Nutrela 15 kg
skuLines.notes: Canteen and mess frying workhorse alongside palmolein. Rate-contract this monthly with the school mess and hostel kitchens rather than selling ad hoc.

skuLines.examples: Fortune Sunlite 1 L, Sundrop 1 L, Gold Winner 1 L, First Crop Sunflower 1 L
skuLines.notes: Second-most-used oil in the North zone (~12% of households). Light, neutral, the default for anyone told to cut down on mustard.

skuLines.line: Refined sunflower oil — 5 L jar and 15 kg tin
skuLines.examples: Fortune Sunlite 5 L, Sundrop 5 L, Gold Winner 15 kg tin
skuLines.notes: Keep the 5 L for households; the tin only if a canteen actually specifies sunflower — otherwise palmolein and soyabean cover institutional frying more cheaply.

skuLines.line: Refined rice bran oil — 1 L / 5 L
skuLines.examples: Fortune Rice Bran Health 1 L, Sundrop Heart, Super Sarvottam 905 g, First Crop Rice Bran 1 L
skuLines.notes: The 'doctor told me to switch' oil — oryzanol/cholesterol positioning. ~9% of North-zone households. In a township with resident elderly and diabetic/cardiac staff this is a genuine must-have, not a health-fad line.

skuLines.examples: Ruchi Gold 850 g, Rajni Gold 800 g, SOR Refined Palmolein, Best Choice 750 g
skuLines.notes: Cheapest oil on the shelf and the entry price point for the tightest household budgets — non-teaching staff. Solidifies partly below ~20 °C, which in a Baru Sahib winter looks like 'the oil has gone bad' to a first-time buyer; put a note on the shelf.

skuLines.examples: Ruchi Gold 15 kg, Raag Gold 15 kg, Sathi Gold 15 kg, Frywell 15 kg, Radhuni 13 kg
skuLines.notes: The single largest-volume fat line in any institutional kitchen — canteen deep-frying (samosa, pakora, puri) and the langar kitchen. Deliberately keep two brands so a single mill's stockout never dries out the mess.

skuLines.examples: Fortune Groundnut 1 L, Safal Refined Groundnut, Dhara Groundnut, Gulab Groundnut 5 L
skuLines.packSizes: 1 L pouch/bottle, 5 L jar, 15 kg tin
skuLines.notes: High smoke point, does not break down on repeat frying — the halwai/sweet-making and Gujarati/Maharashtrian-staff preference. Roughly double mustard's price per litre, so 1 L is the realistic pack here.

skuLines.line: Filtered / kachi ghani groundnut oil (unrefined, aromatic)
skuLines.examples: Safal Filtered Groundnut, Tirupati filtered, Ankur filtered, Dhara filtered
skuLines.notes: Distinct from refined groundnut — nutty aroma, cloudy. Small but loyal demand; single facing. Shorter shelf life than refined.

skuLines.examples: Saffola Gold 1 L, Saffola Total, Sundrop Heart, Fortune Xpert Pro
skuLines.notes: Rice-bran+sunflower / rice-bran+safflower blends. Legally a 'Multi Sourced Edible Vegetable Oil' and must carry the AGMARK mark plus component percentages — check the pack before listing. Cannot contain mustard oil.

skuLines.examples: Saffola Gold 5 L jar (₹1,279 at Vishal Mega Mart, Aug 2026), Saffola Total 5 L, Sundrop 5 L
skuLines.notes: Highest-value household oil pack in the store. Faculty and senior-staff households buy this monthly; it is also the pack most likely to be price-checked against Amazon/BigBasket, so keep the tag honest.

skuLines.examples: India Gate Uplife Gut-Pro (₹191, Blinkit), Saffola Aura Olive & Flaxseed, Fortune Xpert Weight Watchers
skuLines.notes: A genuinely new 2025-26 shelf: KRBL launched Uplife Feb 2025. Aimed at the 18-25 university cohort and health-forward faculty. Low volume, good margin — one facing each.

skuLines.examples: Ginni cottonseed, Tirupati mixed, local mill 'refined vegetable oil' packs
skuLines.notes: Only worth a slot if a supplier gives a real price advantage over palmolein/soyabean; otherwise it just fragments the value shelf. Must be Agmark-labelled if multi-source.

skuLines.line: Coconut oil, edible grade — 500 ml / 1 L jar
skuLines.examples: Parachute 1 L pet jar, Parachute 500 ml, KLF Nirmal, Safal Coconut, Shalimar
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks Apr–Sep; demand shifts to small packs in winter
skuLines.notes: Bought for cooking by South Indian staff AND for hair/body by nearly everyone — dual-use, so it moves faster than its cooking share suggests. HILL CONSTRAINT: coconut oil solidifies below ~24 °C, and Baru Sahib winters run 0–10 °C, so stock WIDE-MOUTH jars, never narrow bottles — a frozen narrow bottle is a returned bottle. Prices have repriced sharply upward (Parachute 1 L ~₹575 in 2026 vs ~₹350 historically) on copra shortage.

skuLines.examples: Parachute 100 ml / 175 ml bottle, Nihar 50 ml, sachets
skuLines.seasonality: Winter-skewed (small packs stay usable when the big jar sets solid)
skuLines.notes: The hostel-student pack — school children 5-18 and university students buy this from pocket money. Also the answer to the winter-solidification problem: a 100 ml bottle warms in the hand, a 1 L block does not.

skuLines.examples: Max Protein VCO, Coco Soul Virgin, KLF Coconad Virgin, Nutriorg
skuLines.notes: MCT/wellness positioning. Single facing; slow-moving at 5,000 residents and 12-month shelf life is tight if throughput is low.

skuLines.line: Sesame / til (gingelly) oil — refined or expeller
skuLines.examples: KLF Tilnad, Idhayam, Anjali Gingelly, Tata Simply Better sesame
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Nov–Jan peak — Lohri and Makar Sankranti (til, gajak, rewri), plus winter massage and oil-pulling
skuLines.notes: In a Punjabi-Sikh institution Lohri (13 Jan) is a real event, and til oil plus til sweets spike around it — plan the indent in November. Also the South Indian staff's tempering oil year-round.

skuLines.examples: Standard Cold Pressed Gingelly, PUVI sesame, Humpy Farms Til cold-pressed (₹249, Zepto), SGR777 chekku
skuLines.notes: Dark, strongly aromatic, used medicinally and for abhyanga massage. One facing, 500 ml only — 3-6 month shelf life.

skuLines.examples: Nutriorg flaxseed oil, Farm Naturelle alsi, Saffola Aura flaxseed blend
skuLines.notes: Omega-3 ALA positioning; NOT for frying — sell as a drizzle/supplement oil and say so on the tag. Very short shelf life (3-6 months) and needs cool, dark storage; the hill cold actually helps here.

skuLines.examples: Figaro Olive Oil 1 L, Leonardo Pomace, Del Monte Pomace (₹592), Borges Pomace
skuLines.notes: ~7% of North-zone households now use olive oil. Pomace is the frying/sauté grade and the honest recommendation for Indian cooking — extra virgin should not be the default sell. Guest-house and faculty demand.

skuLines.examples: Borges EVOO 500 ml (₹520–570), Del Monte EVOO 500 ml (₹598) / 1 L (₹1,077), Figaro EVOO, DiSano
skuLines.notes: Salad and finishing oil. Buyers here are university faculty, visiting academics and the guest house — not the mass base. Deeply discounted online (up to 60% off MRP), so price it realistically or it dies on the shelf. Keep out of light.

skuLines.line: Premium exotic oil — avocado / walnut / rice-bran single-origin
skuLines.examples: DiSano avocado oil, Rowther walnut oil, Nutriorg avocado, Borges avocado
skuLines.notes: Newly trending in India in 2025-26 (avocado-oil claims now appearing even on snack packs). One facing as a statement/gifting SKU — do not carry depth; expiry risk at township throughput.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Badam Tail, Baidyanath badam rogan, Hamdard Roghan Badam Shirin, kalonji oil
skuLines.notes: Sold as a tonic (a spoon in milk) and for scalp/skin — bridges into the ayurvedic shelf. Confirm the pack is food-grade/edible-labelled before selling it as edible; several badam oils are cosmetic-grade only.

skuLines.line: Branded cow ghee — 1 L pouch / tetra / jar
skuLines.examples: Amul Pure Ghee 1 L, Verka Desi Ghee 1 L, Mother Dairy 1 L, Patanjali Cow Ghee 1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Winter peak Oct–Feb; festival peaks at Gurpurab (Nov, Jan), Lohri, Baisakhi, Diwali
skuLines.notes: The highest-value staple in the whole basket and the item residents most resent buying in town. A family of 4 uses 500 ml-1 L/month. GST on ghee fell 12% → 5% on 22 Sep 2025 (GST 2.0) and brands cut MRP by up to ₹40 — verify you are selling post-cut MRP, not old stock printed at 12%.

skuLines.line: Branded cow ghee — 200 ml / 500 ml small pack
skuLines.examples: Amul 200 ml / 500 ml, Verka 500 ml, Patanjali 200 ml, Aashirvaad Svasti 500 ml
skuLines.notes: Hostel-room pack, low-cash-week pack, and the first ghee a young married household buys. Also the weaning pack — a spoon of ghee in khichdi is standard for babies from ~7 months, so this line serves the infant cohort too.

skuLines.line: Branded ghee — 5 L / 15 kg institutional tin
skuLines.examples: Amul 15 kg tin, Verka 15 kg, Mother Dairy 15 kg, Gowardhan 15 L, Patanjali 5 L (4.53 kg) tin
skuLines.priceBand: ₹8,500–11,000 per 15 kg (derived from 1 L pricing, not verified live)
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy peaks at Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Hola Mohalla and all langar/samagam days
skuLines.notes: Karah prasad is made with desi ghee in roughly equal weight to flour and sugar, so a Kalgidhar Trust township's langar and gurdwara kitchen is a large, predictable, contract-able ghee buyer. This is probably the single biggest rupee line in the category — rate-contract it, do not sell it hand-to-mouth.

skuLines.examples: Verka Desi Ghee, Nova, Milkfood, Paras (₹133 small pack, Blinkit), Ananda 850 ml (₹569)
skuLines.packSizes: 500 ml, 1 L, 1 kg, 5 L tin, 15 kg tin
skuLines.notes: Punjab/HP households often prefer granular (danedar) buffalo or mixed-milk ghee over smooth cow ghee — do not assume 'cow ghee' covers the demand. Verka is the co-op brand with the strongest regional trust in this belt.

skuLines.examples: Anveshan Gir cow bilona, Two Brothers Organic Farm, Brahmras, Barosi, Dabur native-breed ghee
skuLines.notes: India's A2 ghee market is forecast to grow ~21% CAGR over 2026-34 and has moved from D2C-only into offline retail. In a religious-institution township this also sells as a gifting and sewa-offering item. 250-500 ml jars only — the 1 L is too big a first purchase.

skuLines.examples: 24 Mantra Organic ghee, Sri Sri Tattva, Patanjali Organic, Organic India
skuLines.notes: Needs a genuine India Organic/Jaivik Bharat mark on the pack. One or two facings; overlaps heavily with the A2 line.

skuLines.examples: Amul ghee 10-15 ml sachets, Aashirvaad Svasti 50 ml, institutional ghee cups
skuLines.packSizes: 9–15 ml sachet, 50 ml cup, cartons of 100
skuLines.notes: For the canteens and Ary Lite counter — a ghee sachet with a paratha or dal thali, sold per unit. Turns a bulk commodity into a per-transaction item and lifts bill value; the two canteens should be buying these by the carton.

skuLines.examples: Desi ghee 1 L for akhand jyot, solidified ghee wicks (ghee batti / diya batti), Amul/Verka jyot-grade ghee
skuLines.packSizes: 200 ml, 500 ml, 1 L; packs of 30-100 ghee wicks
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks at Gurpurab, Diwali/Bandi Chhor Divas, Baisakhi and samagam days
skuLines.notes: A Sikh-institution-specific line ARY is uniquely placed to own: ghee for the jyot at the gurdwara and in staff homes, plus ready-made ghee wicks. Distinct buying decision from cooking ghee (buyers accept a cheaper grade for the lamp, and buy on religious-calendar dates, not monthly).

skuLines.examples: HIMFED / Him Gauri ghee, Verka HP packs, local dairy co-op 1 kg pouch
skuLines.notes: Shorter supply line into the hills than the national brands (lower freight, fresher stock, better margin) and reads as local/trusted. Verify FSSAI licence number and batch dating on every lot — small dairies are the usual source of adulteration complaints.

skuLines.line: Vanaspati (hydrogenated vegetable fat) — 1 L retail pack
skuLines.examples: Dalda Vanaspati 1 L, Rath, Panghat, Gagan, Preet Lite (₹395/1 L)
skuLines.seasonality: Strong winter peak — halwa, pinni, panjiri, gur-based sweets Nov–Feb
skuLines.notes: Still the working household's substitute for ghee at a third of the price, and the fat of choice for halwa and puri. Do not let 'unhealthy' opinions thin this line — for the non-teaching-staff cohort it is a must-have, and the winter sweet season is real volume.

skuLines.examples: Dalda 15 kg tin, Rath 15 kg, Gagan 15 kg, Panghat 15 kg
skuLines.priceBand: ₹2,100–2,900 per tin (derived; wholesale quotes found were stale/inconsistent — verify with the supplier)
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks at Gurpurab/langar and in the winter sweet season
skuLines.notes: The langar and canteen halwa/prasad fat, and the bakery fat if the canteen bakes. Buy on a confirmed current quote — the online 15 kg vanaspati prices in circulation range from ₹1,100 to ₹2,700 and most are years out of date.

skuLines.examples: FFF bakery shortening, Urmison, Leela Foods, Bunge/Adani bakery fats
skuLines.notes: Only if a canteen or the institution's bakery actually makes biscuits, cakes, rusk or patties — check before listing. Palm-based, 15/20 kg cartons, and demand in India is overwhelmingly institutional rather than retail. Store cool and dry; monsoon humidity ruins the carton before the fat.

skuLines.examples: Nutralite spread, Amul Delicious Table Margarine, Milkfood margarine
skuLines.notes: Canteen breakfast/toast use and a cheaper butter substitute for hostel students. Needs chilled or at least cool storage — in a hill store it survives winter easily but wants a cabinet Apr–Sep. Sits on the boundary with the dairy/butter shelf; agree which counter owns it.

skuLines.examples: Saffola oil spray, Nutralite spray, Borges olive oil spray
skuLines.notes: Portion-control novelty for weight-conscious students and faculty. One facing at most; genuinely optional.

skuLines.examples: Amul ghee gift tin, premium ghee + cold-pressed oil combo box, A2 ghee gift jar
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurab (Nov, Dec/Jan), Diwali/Bandi Chhor Divas, Baisakhi, and staff-family wedding season
skuLines.notes: High-margin seasonal build, and in a township ghee is an accepted and appropriate gift and sewa offering. Buy on a firm returns/exchange arrangement — unsold decorative tins are dead stock for a year.

trends2026: GST 2.0 (effective 22 Sep 2025) cut dairy fats including ghee, butter and butter oil from 12% to 5%, and brands passed on up to ₹40 per pack — ghee got structurally cheaper against refined oil for the first time in years, and volume has moved back toward ghee. Any pre-cut MRP stock on the shelf is now a customer-trust problem.

Cold-pressed and wood-pressed ('lakdi ghani', 'chekku') oils are the fastest-premiumising sub-segment — the India cold-pressed oil market was ~₹755 mn in 2025 heading to ~₹1.21 bn by 2034 — driven by an under-35 'return to roots' rejection of refined oil rather than by any price advantage.

A2 / Gir-cow bilona ghee has moved from D2C-only to mainstream offline retail, with the India A2 ghee market forecast to grow at ~21% CAGR over 2026-34 — the highest-growth premium line in the whole category.

Coconut oil has repriced sharply upward on copra shortage: Parachute 1 L was quoted around ₹575 in 2026 against a historic ~₹350, pushing buyers down into 175-500 ml packs and making the small-pack shelf more important than the jar shelf.

Functional and claim-led oil blends went mainstream in 2025-26 — KRBL launched 'India Gate Uplife' Gut-Pro blends in Feb 2025, and Saffola Aura pushes olive+flaxseed — so the health claim now sits on the oil's own label rather than only on the brand's reputation.

Regulatory tightening on loose oil is being actively enforced: FSSAI permits multi-source edible oil only in tamper-proof sealed packs of at most 15 kg, and the Maharashtra FDA publicly banned loose/unpacked edible oil sale in August 2026 with penalties up to 7 years — the traditional hill-store practice of decanting from a drum is now a prosecutable offence, not a grey area.

The FSSAI ban on blending mustard oil with any other oil (in force since 8 Jun 2021) has hardened into a pure-play mustard market — every mustard SKU must be 100% mustard, and any 'blend' pack on a shelf today is either non-compliant or old stock.

Pouches now hold ~52% of the Indian mustard oil market as price-sensitive buyers chase the lowest cost per litre, while the 5 L jar consolidates the monthly stock-up — the middle formats (2 L, 3 L) are being squeezed out from both sides.

Premium exotic oils — avocado, walnut, flaxseed — have crossed from niche health stores into modern trade, and avocado oil is now used as a claim on finished snacks (e.g. an avocado-oil sev range launched in 2026), pulling consumer awareness of the ingredient ahead of actual cooking use.
adjacentServices: Monthly rate-contract institutional supply to the school mess, university hostel kitchens, the langar/gurdwara kitchen and the two canteens — indent-based, fixed price for the month, 15 kg tins of palmolein, soyabean, vanaspati and desi ghee. This is the largest rupee opportunity in the category and it should not be sold hand-to-mouth.

Standing supply of jyot ghee and ready-made ghee wicks to the gurdwara, keyed to the religious calendar (Gurpurab, Bandi Chhor Divas, Baisakhi, Hola Mohalla, samagam days) rather than to a monthly cycle.

Free in-township home delivery of 5 L jars and 15 kg tins — oil and ghee are the heaviest, bulkiest items in the basket, and delivery is what converts a resident from buying 1 L at a time to buying the monthly pack.
Standing order / subscription on the household staple pair (one 5 L oil jar + one 1 L ghee pack per month) with a fixed delivery date, billed to a staff account.
Salary-deduction or monthly credit account for staff households, so the ₹1,000-plus oil-and-ghee purchase does not have to land in one cash week.
Empty tin, jar and jerrycan buyback with a return deposit — cuts waste in a closed township, and 15 kg tins have real resale value that currently leaks out.

Used cooking oil (UCO) collection from the canteens, mess and langar kitchen under FSSAI's RUCO framework, aggregated and sold to a biodiesel collector — turns a disposal cost and a food-safety risk (repeat frying) into revenue.

A visible price-comparison board showing ARY's shelf price per litre against the current rate in the nearest market town for the top 10 oil and ghee SKUs — the cheapest way to stop the 'town is cheaper' wallet leak on the single most price-checked category in the store.

Fry-oil discipline support for the canteens: no-repeat-frying guidance, a simple TPC (total polar compounds) check, and a scheduled oil-change indent — a food-safety service the institution needs and no one else there sells.
Festival and Gurpurab ghee gift packs plus a 'buy ghee here, it goes to the langar' sewa-donation counter — a natural, high-margin seasonal build for a Kalgidhar Trust township.
Group buying of a 15 kg tin split across several staff families at the tin's per-litre price, sold as sealed retail packs alongside it — never by decanting the tin, which is illegal.
